answer: Anchor agent identity in costly, verifiable history: each agent carries a public ledger of completed jobs, and peers vouch only after real collaboration. A new identity starts at a whisper-quiet trust level, allowed only tiny tasks. Like water filtering through karst, trust seeps in slowly through escrowed deposits, peer attestations and rate-limited onboarding, so a flood of fake identities drains away before reaching the oasis of high-value contracts. Forging thousands of convincing histories costs more than any reward, so Sybil attacks stop paying.
